en: Mayon Volcano in Albay has a six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone to protect residents from deadly lava flows and ash.
Coastal towns in Eastern Samar face the Pacific Ocean and must prepare evacuation plans for potential destructive tsunami waves.
The Sierra Madre mountain range acts as a natural barrier, blocking strong typhoon winds from reaching central Luzon.
The Pasig River in Metro Manila contains high levels of industrial pollution, making its water unsafe for swimming.
Tuguegarao frequently records the highest temperatures in the Philippines, so residents must drink water to prevent dangerous heatstroke.
During the wet season, stagnant floodwaters in low-lying Manila neighborhoods breed mosquitoes that transmit the dangerous dengue virus.
Nighttime temperatures on Mount Pulag in Benguet drop below freezing, requiring hikers to wear thick jackets to prevent hypothermia.
Drinking untreated water from the Agusan River in Mindanao can expose you to harmful bacteria causing severe diarrhea.
Building houses on the steep slopes of the Cordillera mountains increases the risk of deadly landslides during heavy rains.
Strong ultraviolet rays at Philippine beaches like Boracay can cause severe sunburns, so wearing sunscreen protects your skin.
Swimmers in the Sulu Sea must avoid box jellyfish, whose venomous tentacles can deliver painful and dangerous stings.
Kaingin farming in the Cordillera highlands produces thick smoke that travels to lowlands, triggering asthma attacks in children.
